summary: H. E. Colvile, an officer of the Guards, went out to Egypt late in 1883 to look at the Wady el Arabah, the valley that runs from the Gulf of Akabah towards the Dead Sea. With Arab guides and camels he crossed the Sinai peninsula from Suez to Akabah, surveyed and levelled part of the Arabah, considered the line for a railway, and came back across the Tih plateau by Nakh’l to Suez. He writes lightly of the guides, the camels, and his own mishaps, and gives his observations of the ground, with a few geological sections. A sketch map shows his route, and an appendix gives the itineraries.
